```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {selectControl, loadWeekData, weekIssueTimeline, skillByLead, weekSkillMaps, weekIssueMaps, weekSeries} from "../assets/leads/leads.js"
weekData = loadWeekData("../assets/week-leads-2023/")
geo = ({indonesia: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/indonesia.geojson").json(),
  provinces: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/provinces.geojson").json(),
  neighbours: await FileAttachment("../data/boundaries/neighbours.geojson").json()})
issueChoices = weekData.issues.map(d => [d.issued, `Issued ${d.label}${d.targets.length < weekData.leads.length ? ` (${d.targets.length} of ${weekData.leads.length} leads in October-December)` : ""}`])
```

::: {.eyebrow}
Case 06 · Lead time · Subseasonal rainfall by week · Full Indonesia at 0.05°
:::

Every Wednesday a forecaster can ask: how much rain will fall in **each of the
next four weeks**, and over **weeks 3 and 4** together? This case builds that
forecast for October-December 2023 over Indonesia from **GEFSv12**, calibrated
with CCA and PCR through CPT, and measures how much skill is left one to four
weeks ahead.

Unlike the other cases, it works at the **native 0.05° grid** of CHIRPS v3.0:
61,190 pixels over Indonesia instead of 3,240 cells of 0.25°. All numbers on this
page come from the [executed notebook](../notebooks/week-leads-2023.ipynb).

Hover, tap or use the arrow keys on any map or chart to read values; each view can
be downloaded as it is set. Maps load when you choose them, one small file per map.

::: {.callout-note title="The short result"}
- Skill falls with each week: the area-mean CCA correlation is **0.35** for week 1,
  0.29 for week 2, 0.26 for week 3 and **0.17** for week 4. Weeks 3-4 together
  score 0.26, about the same as week 3 alone and well above week 4.
- The **raw GEFSv12** correlation is clearly higher for weeks 1 and 2 (0.50 and
  0.34). From week 3 on, raw and calibrated differ by at most 0.01.
- In late 2023 the weeks were **drier than normal** (below normal over 49% of the
  pixel-weeks). The forecasts leaned dry, beat climatological odds at every lead
  (RPSS 0.07 to 0.14), and matched the hit rate of "always below normal" for
  weeks 1, 2 and 3-4 while falling short of it for weeks 3 and 4.
:::

## How a weekly forecast is issued

A forecast is issued at 00 UTC on a Wednesday, from the GEFSv12 run started then.
Model day *d* covers the same 24 hours as observed day issue + *d*, so the targets
are simple windows of days after the issue date:

| Lead | Days after issue | Training targets | Latest model day |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 1 | 1-7 | 249 | 7 |
| Week 2 | 8-14 | 249 | 14 |
| Week 3 | 15-21 | 249 | 21 |
| Week 4 | 22-28 | 249 | 28 |
| Weeks 3-4 | 15-28 | 249 | 28 |

Weeks 3-4 is the period of NOAA CPC's
[week 3-4 outlook](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/WK34/),
days 15 to 28 after issue. GEFSv12's hindcasts (2000-2018) also start on
Wednesdays, so training uses exactly the same leads as real time; the dekad case
needed a compromise here, this one does not. The training targets are every
window starting on a Thursday in October-December 2000-2018, 13 or 14 per year;
each has one start per lead, so all five leads are trained and scored on the same
249 targets. A week 5 would need model day 35, beyond the run.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof timelineIssue = selectControl("Issue date", issueChoices, "2023-11-01")
weekIssueTimeline(weekData, timelineIssue)
```
:::

## Daily observations at 0.05°

The observations are **daily CHIRPS v3.0** (the `rnl` variant), exported for
Indonesia from Earth Engine and converted to yearly NetCDF files by the tutorial's
[`gee_daily_to_netcdf.py`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial/blob/main/research/scripts/gee_daily_to_netcdf.py).
As a check, their sums over three dekads (2005, 2012 and 2023) equal the dekadal
archive used by the other cases to within 0.0001 mm at every Indonesian pixel,
with the same missing pixels. A weekly total is the sum of its seven days (14 for
weeks 3-4); the notebook asserts that every day of every window is present.

::: {.callout-warning title="Daily CHIRPS is not an independent daily product"}
CHC builds daily CHIRPS v3.0 from the pentad product: each pentad's amount is shared
between its days using the timing of ERA5 (the `rnl` variant used here) or IMERG,
with no separate daily station blending, and CHC recommends pentadal or longer
totals wherever the science allows
([CHIRPS daily readme](https://data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS/v3.0/daily/readme.txt)).
These weeks run Thursday to Wednesday and so cut across pentads: how much of a
pentad's rain falls inside a week comes from ERA5's timing, not from stations. The
weekly totals, and the skill measured against them, carry that dependence; how much
it matters was not measured here. The same readme notes that the daily dates follow
ERA5's UTC days (00 to 00 UTC), while the stations behind the pentad totals do not
all report on UTC days, so the match with GEFSv12's model days is approximate. The
[pentad case](pentad-leads-2023.qmd) uses the pentad product itself.
:::

Rainfall rises through October-December, so model and observations are turned into
**anomalies** before fitting. A target's mean is the average of 19 training
targets of the same lead, one from each year 2000-2018: the one starting closest to
the same day of the season. On average their start is 1.7 days from the target's,
at most 6 days. Each forecast **total** is that mean for the observations plus the
calibrated anomaly, set to zero where the sum is negative. The 2000-2018 mean over
Indonesian pixels is 64.1 mm a week (129.2 mm for weeks 3-4).

## Skill falls with each week

CCA (3 predictor and 3 predictand EOFs, 2 CCA modes) and PCR (3 predictor EOFs)
are fitted at each lead through `cptcore`, the layer PyCPT's `evaluate_models`
calls, with cross-validation leaving out 27 targets at a time (the held-out week
and 13 on each side, about a season). At 0.05° one fit took 76 to 90 minutes for
CCA and 23 to 26 minutes for PCR, so the ten fits ran in parallel, in 90 minutes.
For every fit, CPT's correlation map equals the correlation recomputed from its own
cross-validated hindcasts to within 0.000001.

**Pearson correlation** is 0 for no linear relationship; **2AFC** is the chance
that the forecast ranks two different weeks in the observed order, 50% for no
skill [(Mason and Weigel 2009)](https://doi.org/10.1175/2008MWR2553.1).

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof skillMetric = selectControl("Score", [["Pearson", "Pearson correlation"], ["2AFC (%)", "2AFC"]], "Pearson")
skillByLead(weekData, skillMetric)
```
:::

| Lead | CCA Pearson | PCR Pearson | Raw GEFS Pearson | CCA 2AFC (%) | PCR 2AFC (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 1 | 0.35 | 0.36 | 0.50 | 62.8 | 63.1 |
| Week 2 | 0.29 | 0.28 | 0.34 | 60.3 | 60.3 |
| Week 3 | 0.26 | 0.26 | 0.25 | 59.6 | 59.6 |
| Week 4 | 0.17 | 0.18 | 0.18 | 56.7 | 56.8 |
| Weeks 3-4 | 0.26 | 0.26 | 0.25 | 59.6 | 59.7 |

: Area-weighted means over 61,190 pixels, 249 targets of 2000-2018. Source: [skill-by-lead.csv](../data/week-leads-2023/skill-by-lead.csv).

1. **Skill falls with lead, most between weeks 3 and 4.** CCA's mean correlation
   drops by 0.06 from week 1 to 2, 0.02 from week 2 to 3, and 0.09 from week 3 to 4.
2. **Two weeks together hold up better than the second of them.** Weeks 3-4 score
   0.26, close to week 3 and well above week 4 alone (0.17).
3. **Calibration does not beat the raw model.** GEFSv12's own anomaly correlates
   better in weeks 1 and 2 (by 0.15 and 0.05 over CCA) and about equally from
   week 3. As in the other cases, the calibrated scores pay a cross-validation cost
   [(Barnston and van den Dool 1993)](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(1993)006%3C0963:ADICVS%3E2.0.CO;2)
   and see the model only through 3 EOF patterns; neither effect was measured here.
4. **CCA and PCR are nearly identical**, within 0.01 at every lead.

## The forecasts as issued in late 2023

Sixteen Wednesdays, from 13 September to 27 December 2023, issued at least one
forecast whose target falls in October-December; ten of them, 4 October to
6 December, cover all five leads. Choose an issue date, the calibration and what
to show; each map is one lead against its own target.

::: {.story-interactive}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mapIssue = selectControl("Issue date", issueChoices, "2023-11-01")
viewof issueMethod = selectControl("Calibration", [["CCA", "CCA"], ["PCR", "PCR"]], "CCA")
viewof issueView = selectControl("Show", [["total", "Forecast total"], ["observed", "Observed total"], ["difference", "Forecast minus observed"], ["category", "Most likely category"], ["observedCategory", "Observed category"]], "total")
weekIssueMaps(weekData, geo, mapIssue, issueMethod, issueView)
```
:::

Over the 13 targets of each lead, scored over every pixel and target
(area-weighted):

| Lead | Method | Hit rate (%) | Reference (%) | RPSS 2023 | RMSE 2023 (mm) | Mean forecast (mm) | Observed mean (mm) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Week 1 | CCA | 50.4 | 49.4 | 0.12 | 28.6 | 55.7 | 51.1 |
| Week 1 | PCR | 49.5 | 49.4 | 0.12 | 28.8 | 55.7 | 51.1 |
| Week 2 | CCA | 50.2 | 49.4 | 0.12 | 28.5 | 56.0 | 51.1 |
| Week 2 | PCR | 49.6 | 49.4 | 0.11 | 28.7 | 55.7 | 51.1 |
| Week 3 | CCA | 46.8 | 49.4 | 0.07 | 29.7 | 58.0 | 51.1 |
| Week 3 | PCR | 45.9 | 49.4 | 0.07 | 29.7 | 57.8 | 51.1 |
| Week 4 | CCA | 45.6 | 49.4 | 0.08 | 29.8 | 57.8 | 51.1 |
| Week 4 | PCR | 44.8 | 49.4 | 0.07 | 30.0 | 57.7 | 51.1 |
| Weeks 3-4 | CCA | 53.2 | 52.2 | 0.14 | 48.3 | 117.5 | 106.5 |
| Weeks 3-4 | PCR | 51.1 | 52.2 | 0.13 | 48.7 | 117.4 | 106.5 |

: October-December 2023. Source: [ond-2023-weekly-forecasts.csv](../data/week-leads-2023/ond-2023-weekly-forecasts.csv).

- **Hit rate** is the share where the most likely category was the one observed.
  The **reference** is always forecasting the most frequent observed category,
  below normal (49.4% of one-week pixel-targets, 52.2% for weeks 3-4). Weeks 1, 2
  and 3-4 matched it to within about a point; weeks 3 and 4 fell 2.5 to 4.5 points
  short.
- **RPSS 2023** compares the forecast probabilities with climatological odds
  (33/34/33%) using the ranked probability score
  [(Epstein 1969)](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1969)008%3C0985:ASSFPF%3E2.0.CO;2):
  positive at every lead, highest for weeks 3-4 and weeks 1-2. One season of
  13 weeks rewards leaning the right way in 2023, not skill in general.
- **The totals were too wet** on average: 55.7 to 58.0 mm a week against an observed
  51.1 mm, although the most likely category was below normal over 58% to 73% of
  the area.

## What this does and does not show

This is one season of weeks, one model, one set of fixed settings, 19 training
years and one verifying season. It shows that, for GEFSv12 weekly rainfall over
Indonesia in October-December at 0.05°, skill falls from 0.35 to 0.17 over four
weeks, that combining weeks 3 and 4 keeps more skill than week 4 alone, and that
calibration with these settings did not add to the raw model's correlation. The
observations are retrospective CHIRPS v3.0, not what was available when each
forecast was issued, and the 2023 forecasts average 31 GEFSv12 members while the
hindcasts have 11.

The [dekad case](dekad-leads-2023.qmd) asks the same question by dekad at 0.25°.
